title: Isoniazid oral solution, USP: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Chartwell RX, LLC)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration approved prescribing information, via DailyMed; version 2, effective 2 December 2025
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Isoniazid is metabolised primarily by acetylation and dehydrazination, and the rate of acetylation is genetically determined. The rate does not significantly alter the effectiveness of isoniazid, but slow acetylation may lead to higher blood concentrations and so to an increase in toxic reactions. Peripheral neuropathy is the most common toxic effect and its incidence is higher in slow inactivators. Peak blood concentrations decline to 50% or less within 6 hours, and 50% to 70% of a dose is excreted in the urine within 24 hours. The label also notes pyridoxine deficiency with high doses, ascribed to competition with pyridoxal phosphate, and carries a boxed warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatitis.
